summary: One of the first Great Lakes lights (1818), at Erie, PA: rebuilt in brick, then sandstone; kept until 1899; now a city park with a climbable tower in season.

lens.note: Third-order Fresnel from 1867; the lantern room was removed after the last keeper left (LighthouseFriends gives no date; it went to Marblehead Lighthouse, Ohio). USLHS lists the optic as removed.

structures.note: The 1818 stone tower was replaced by a brick tower (1857-58) and then by this one; it stands 49 ft (15 m)

access.note: Grounds open daily from dawn to dusk; the tower can be climbed on set days in season.

corrections.why: The standing tower dates from 1867. The 1818 tower was replaced by brick towers in 1857-58 and 1867 (LighthouseFriends, Port Authority). The record's 1818 date belongs to the first tower, not this one.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: LighthouseFriends describes a twenty-foot stone tower with an iron lantern; the Port Authority says the 1818 tower was built of wood. The story follows LighthouseFriends and records the disagreement.
The Port Authority dates the first rebuild to 1857; LighthouseFriends places the new dwelling in 1858 and does not give a completion year for the brick tower in the passage read.
The USLHS roster gives 1819-1833; LighthouseFriends gives 1818-1832. Both are kept in the story.

notes_for_editor: The NRHP nomination 78002397 is not digitised (the npgallery PDF is a placeholder), so it was not read. The HABS record (loc.gov item pa0452) returned 403 and was not read; loc.gov is used only through newspapers.py. Chronicling America searches for the 1881 sale, the 1885 relighting and the 1899 closure gave only unrelated pages, so no newspaper is cited. The 1891 Board item (item 1091) is in the report for the fiscal year ended June 30, 1891, not 1891-92: the volume's title page and the page header 'REPORT OF THE LIGHT-HOUSE BOARD. 137' confirm printed page 137; the Internet Archive page index gives scan page 188. The item's heading reads 'Erie, outside of Erie Harbor, Presque Isle Bay' and names no light; the attribution to Erie Land is an inference from the heading and the keeper's dwelling. The same report lists the Presque Isle north-pier light separately (items 1092 and 1095), which is why the story says the link is an inference. LighthouseFriends is all-rights-reserved: facts are paraphrased and quoted at most in short phrases. Keeper names and dates come from the USLHS roster (NARA registers via the Kraig Anderson inventory); the roster person slugs were checked against roster.py output. No primary record confirming each name was read. The roster and LighthouseFriends disagree on John Bone's dates. The record's first_lit 1818 is kept; the structure's built date is corrected to 1867. 2021 control and City of Erie ownership come only from LighthouseFriends; the 2021 agreement was for two years, so it may have lapsed. Check with the Port Authority or the City before a visit. No storm, wreck or rescue tied to this light was found in the corpus or the sources read, so the chapter is omitted. LighthouseFriends says George W. Miller came from Conneaut Lighthouse after sixteen years but gives no dates, so no other_stations entry is made. Wikipedia was read only as a lead and is not cited.
